_comment: How the spec's Einsum labels map onto the IR, and the few structural
facts the IR does not carry.
setup / body: which labels run once before the loop and which run once
per generation. The IR lists the cascade's Einsums in order but does
not say where the loop begins -- E01..E05 build the preflow and the
residual graph from the input and never run again, while E06..E24 are
the repeated step.
A LIST of indices means the label is one written Einsum that had to be
lowered to several IR nodes. E04 is a three-arm `cases`; the arms run
in order and each overwrites the last, which is what makes the u=s arm
win. The reader wrote one Einsum, so the trace shows one step.
stopAfter: where in the round the stopping condition is tested. The IR
says WHAT to test; it does not say where the loop is cut. Testing
after E06 rather than at the end of the round is the same algorithm --
E06 computes Act from the current excess, and so does E19 -- but it
changes the trace: a run that stops shows a short final generation
(E06, then stop) instead of a full one.
selectors: choice function name -> the rule this run uses. Required: an
unmapped name stops the cascade rather than being guessed at.
pick-admissible-edge is genuinely free: the Einsum is written
1(pick-admissible-edge), which says ANY admissible edge, and any one of
them is a legal push. So the default is seeded-random, not a rule.
A deterministic rule would be wrong here in two ways. It would make the
specification claim something it does not -- that the lowest-numbered
neighbour is the one to push to -- and it would sample the space of legal
executions with a bias, so a bug that only shows up on some choices could
never appear. Random is what `any` means.
Seeded rather than unseeded so a build is reproducible: the same seed
gives the same page. The seed sweep in tests/drive_and_compare.js is what
turns `the choice is free` from an assertion into a measurement -- many
seeds, same maximum flow, different work.
Where two implementations are COMPARED the choice has to be pinned, or a
legitimate difference in an unspecified choice looks like disagreement.
That pinning lives in the tests, not here.
displayNames: tensors the spec names one way and the write-up another. The interpreter aliases on read; the driver has to alias on write too, or Delta and delta become two tensors that never meet.
